author: nickyeow

text: 唔使急，仲有大把時間。

english.text: I'll let you know when it has been decided.

jyutping: kyut3 ding6 zo2 ngo5 zau6 wui5 waa6 bei2 nei5 teng1 gaa3 laa3。

english.text: Would you speak more slowly, please?

jyutping: nei5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 gong2 maan6 siu2 siu2 aa3？

author: nickyeow

english.text: Put your name on the notebook in case you forget it.

jyutping: hai2 bun2 bou6 dou6 se2 faan2 nei5 go3 ming4 laa1，m4 sai2 geng1 zing2 m4 gin3 aa1 maa3。
text: 喺本簿度寫返你個名啦，唔使驚整唔見吖嘛。

author: nickyeow

english.text: What is it?

jyutping: ni1 go3 me1 lai4 gaa3？
text: 呢個咩嚟㗎？

author: nickyeow

english.text: "Thank you for helping me." "Don't mention it."

jyutping: 「m4 goi1 saai3 nei5 wo3。」「m4 sai2 m4 goi1。」
text: 「唔該晒你喎。」「唔使唔該。」

author: nickyeow

english.text: Shall we take a short rest?

jyutping: ngo5 dei6 bat1 jyu4 tau2 zan6 sin1 laa1。
text: 我哋不如唞陣先啦。

author: nickyeow

english.text: In spite of all the cooking shows I've watched, I'm still no good in the kitchen.

jyutping: seoi1 jin4 ngo5 tai2 zo2 hou2 do1 paang1 jam6 zit3 muk6，daan6 hai6 ngo5 zyu2 je5 sik6 dou1 zung6 hai6 m4 hai6 hou2 dim6。

author: nickyeow

english.text: My mother is reading a magazine.

jyutping: ngo5 aa3 maa1 hai2 dou6 tai2 gan2 zaap6 zi3。
text: 我阿媽喺度睇緊雜誌。

author: nickyeow

english.text: We wouldn't be in this mess if you'd just done what I told you.

jyutping: jyu4 gwo2 nei5 ziu3 zyu6 ngo5 ge3 syut3 waa6 heoi3 zou6，ngo5 dei6 ji4 gaa1 zau6 m4 wui5 gaau2 sing4 gam2 laa1。

author: nickyeow

english.text: My nose is itchy.

jyutping: ngo5 go3 bei6 hou2 han4。
text: 我個鼻好痕。

english.text: My father is always busy.

jyutping: ngo5 go3 lou5 dau6 seng4 jat6 dou1 hou2 mong4。

author: nickyeow

english.text: How dare you speak to me like that!

jyutping: nei5 ging2 jin4 gau3 daam2 gam3 joeng2 tung4 ngo5 gong2 je5！
text: 你竟然夠膽咁樣同我講嘢！

author: cc_neko

english.text: He isn't at home, is he?

jyutping: keoi5 m4 hai2 uk1 kei2 o3 ho2?
text: 佢唔喺屋企哦可?

author: fercheung

english.text: Tom can run fast.

jyutping: aa3 Tom paau2 dak1 hou2 faai3。
text: 阿Tom跑得好快。

english.text: I don't want to live on this planet anymore.

jyutping: bat1 jyu4 jat1 coeng1 daa2 sei2 ngo5。

english.text: In the English world of the 19th century, it was often said that masturbation would lead to a loss of memory and attention.

We aren't always at home on Mondays.

english.text: It is evident from what has been said, that before 500 A.D. literary chronology, even in the Sanskrit period, is almost entirely relative, priority or posteriority being determined by such criteria as development of style or thought, the mention of earlier authors by name, stray political references as to the Greeks or to some well-known dynasty, and allusions to astronomical facts which cannot have been known before a certain epoch.

text: 由所講嘅可以明顯睇到，喺公元500年之前，即使喺梵文時期，文學年代學幾乎完全係相對嘅，優先次序或後繼性係由風格或思想嘅發展、以名提及早期作者等標準決定。 有關希臘人或者某啲出名嘅王朝嘅流浪政治提及，同埋對某個時代之前唔可能知道嘅天文事實嘅暗示。

english.text: It is sickness to be obsessed with winning, it is sickness to be obsessed with using the martial arts, and it is sickness to be obsessed with putting forth all one has learned. It is sickness to be obsessed with offense, and it is also sickness to be obsessed with defense. It is also sickness to be obsessed with getting rid of sickness. To fix the mind obsessively on anything is considered sickness.

text: 痴住贏係病，痴住用武術係病，痴住將所有學到嘅嘢都放出嚟係病。執着於進攻係一種病，而執着於防守亦都係一種病，執着於擺脫任何嘢都係一種病。亦都係病，痴迷於擺脫病，將心靈痴迷於任何事情上，都算係病。

author: Davidgo5867

english.text: Forty-four US Americans have now taken the presidential oath. The words have been spoken during rising tides of prosperity and the still waters of peace. Yet, every so often, the oath is taken amidst gathering clouds and raging storms. At these moments, America has carried on not simply because of the skill or vision of those in high office, but because We the People have remained faithful to the ideals of our forebearers, and true to our founding documents.

author: Davidgo5867

english.text: In the gardens of the better classes summer-houses and shelters of rustic appearance and diminutive proportions are often seen. Rustic arbors are also to be seen in the larger gardens. Specially constructed houses of quaint design and small size are not uncommon; in these the ceremonial tea-parties take place. High fences, either of board or bamboo, or solid walls of mud or tile with stone foundations, surround the house or enclose it from the street. Low rustic fences border the gardens in the suburbs. Gateways of various styles, some of imposing design, form the entrances; as a general thing they are either rustic and light, or formal and massive.

text: 喺上流社會嘅花園入面，經常會見到外觀同比例細小嘅避暑別墅同避難所。喺較大嘅花園入面亦都可以見到農村風嘅喬木。特別建造嘅屋，設計古怪，面積細，唔罕見；喺呢啲地方，會舉行儀式性嘅茶會。郊區嘅花園有低矮嘅農村圍欄。各種風格嘅閘道，有啲設計壯觀，形成入口；一般嚟講，佢哋一係就質樸同輕盈，一係就正式同巨大。

author: Davidgo5867

english.text: It's a grey cloudy morning this summer day of the 22nd of June of 2025. Before dawn, I had a snack of two tofu fish cuttlefish corn potato tangerine pork rolls with strawberries. Around 8, I was at Starbucks café, there to drink Passion Tango iced tea, which contained hibiscus, lemongrass, cinnamon, passion fruit, pineapple, and so forth. I waited for my religious Baptist Filipino friend, Greg, who was there usually on Sundays at that time, but he didn't show up. Then, I walked to Tim Hortons café to drink an iced coffee with oat milk and eat a sausage English muffin. There were families. There were several ex-Soviet bachelors who spoke Russian. Before 10, I trekked towards the Roman Catholic church at St. Albans Road. I admired the bamboo grove and the Emerald Tree on the way. At the church, there were already some worshippers in the nave: many Filipinos, and some Hispanics and Cantonese. The Filipina nun in her habit was talking to some Filipinas in the lobby area. They were admiring someone's blue skirt, which cost 80 dollars. Today, this morning, many blue hydrangeas adorned the front of the nave, inside. (There is interest in Interlingua.) Yesterday and today counted as my 50th and 51st visits to that church, the "Clam Temple" as I call it because of its architecture. Some people wore beige, an interest in Chabacano. When I walk outside, I usually talk to rabbits in Lojban: "coico'o ractu" (Hello-bye rabbits!). I'm often like Dr. Dolittle.

text: 2025年6月22號呢個夏日，係一個灰暗多雲嘅朝早。喺黎明之前，我食咗兩個豆腐魚墨魚粟米薯仔橘子豬肉卷配士多啤梨嘅小食。點幾，我喺星巴克咖啡館，喺嗰度飲咗熱情探戈冰茶，入面有芙蓉、檸檬草、肉桂、熱情果、菠蘿等等。我等咗我個宗教浸信會菲律賓朋友 Greg ，佢嗰陣通常星期日都會喺度，但係佢冇出現。之後，我行去 Tim Hortons 咖啡廳飲咗杯凍咖啡加燕麥奶，同埋食咗個香腸英式鬆餅。當時有家庭。有幾個前蘇聯嘅單身漢都係講俄文。喺十點前，我行咗去聖阿爾本斯道嘅羅馬天主教教堂。我喺途中欣賞咗竹林同翡翠樹。喺教堂，正殿入面已經有啲崇拜者：好多菲律賓人，同埋有啲西班牙裔同香港人。個菲律賓修女喺佢嘅習慣入面，喺大堂區同啲菲律賓人傾緊計。佢哋喺度欣賞緊某人嘅藍色裙，呢條裙要80文。今日，今朝，好多藍色嘅繡球花裝飾咗正殿前面，入面。 （對國際語言有興趣。）尋日同今日都算係我第50同第51次去嗰間教堂，因為佢嘅建築，我叫佢做「蛤蜊廟」。有啲人着米色，係對查巴卡諾嘅興趣。我行出去嘅時候，通常會同洛伊班嘅兔仔傾偈：「 coico ' o racctu 」（兔仔你好！）。我成日都好似多利特爾博士噉。

author: Davidgo5867

english.text: My experience with diachronic ("through time") telepathy makes me believe that time may not be linear. One theorizes that psychonic or tachyonic particles or waves are faster than light, so that they can travel back in time. (Men like to explain away things, even if they do not understand fully. Women think that they need not understand how something works.)

jyutping: ngo5 deoi3 lik6 si4（「tau3 gwo3 si4 gaan3」）din6 ci4 gam2 jing3 ge3 ging1 jim6 ling6 ngo5 soeng1 seon3 si4 gaan1 mei6 bit1 hai6 sin3 sing3 ge3。jau5 jan4 lei5 leon6 waa6 zing1 san4 lap1 zi2 waak6 ze2 cuk1 dou6 lap1 zi2 waak6 ze2 bo1 hai6 faai3 gwo3 di1 gwong1，so2 ji5 keoi5 dei6 ho2 ji5 faan1 heoi3 gwo3 heoi3。 （naam4 jan2 zung1 ji3 gaai2 sik1 di1 je5，zau6 syun3 keoi5 dei6 m4 jyun4 cyun4 ming4 baak6。neoi5 jan4 gok3 dak1 keoi5 dei6 m4 seoi1 jiu3 ming4 baak6 di1 je5 hai6 dim2 joeng2 wan6 zok3。）
text: 我對歷時（「透過時間」）電磁感應嘅經驗令我相信時間未必係線性嘅。有人理論話精神粒子或者速度粒子或者波係快過啲光，所以佢哋可以返去過去。 （男人鍾意解釋啲嘢，就算佢哋唔完全明白。女人覺得佢哋唔需要明白啲嘢係點樣運作。）

english.text: "Do you know why Yumi is off work today?" "Ah, it seems her cat ran away from home." "Huh? Is it ok for her to do that?" "Of course, it's her paid leave. There were some documents I was going to ask her for, so I'll need you to get them by the end of the day." "Alright."

text: 「你知唔知點解今日由美放工？」「啊，佢隻貓好似係離家出走。」嘩？佢咁做得唔得㗎？」「當然係佢有薪假啦。有啲文件我要問佢，所以我需要你喺日尾攞到佢哋。」「好啦。」

english.text: She was silent, and he went on with increasing vehemence: “I am still that Edgar Ravenswood who, for your affection, renounced the dear ties by which injured honour bound him to seek vengeance. I am that Ravenswood who, for your sake, forgave, nay, clasped hands in friendship with, the oppressor and pillager of his house, the traducer and murderer of his father.”

text: 佢沉默咗，而佢越嚟越激烈噉繼續講：「我仍然係埃德加 · 拉文斯伍德，為咗你嘅感情，放棄咗受傷嘅名譽綁住佢去尋求復仇嘅親愛關係。我就係嗰個拉文斯伍德，為咗你，原諒咗，唔係，同佢屋企嘅壓迫者同掠奪者、佢父親嘅謀殺者、佢父親嘅謀殺者、佢父親嘅謀殺者、佢嘅父親。」
